classification.difficultyReason: Combine a given ratio with sign or domain information, find a missing triangle side and evaluate a second ratio, including reciprocal ratios and surds.

answer.worked:
$\alpha$ is in quadrant IV, so $\tan\alpha<0$. A reference triangle has adjacent side $4$ and hypotenuse $5$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Opposite}&=\sqrt{5^2-4^2}\\&=3\\\tan\alpha&=-\frac34\end{aligned}$$

$\alpha$ is in quadrant II, so $\cos\alpha<0$. A reference triangle has opposite side $8$ and adjacent side $15$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Hypotenuse}&=\sqrt{8^2+15^2}\\&=17\\\cos\alpha&=-\frac{15}{17}\end{aligned}$$

$\alpha$ is in quadrant II, so $\cos\alpha<0$. A reference triangle has opposite side $1$ and hypotenuse $4$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Adjacent}&=\sqrt{4^2-1^2}\\&=\sqrt{15}\\\cos\alpha&=-\frac{\sqrt{15}}4\end{aligned}$$

$\theta$ is in quadrant I, so $\sin\theta>0$. A reference triangle has opposite side $35$ and adjacent side $12$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Hypotenuse}&=\sqrt{35^2+12^2}\\&=37\\\sin\theta&=\frac{35}{37}\end{aligned}$$

$\theta$ is in quadrant II, so $\sec\theta<0$.

$$\sin\theta=\frac23$$

A reference triangle has opposite side $2$ and hypotenuse $3$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Adjacent}&=\sqrt{3^2-2^2}\\&=\sqrt5\\\sec\theta&=-\frac3{\sqrt5}\end{aligned}$$

$$\cos\theta=-\frac8{17}$$

The domain places $\theta$ in quadrant II, so $\tan\theta<0$. A reference triangle has adjacent side $8$ and hypotenuse $17$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Opposite}&=\sqrt{17^2-8^2}\\&=15\\\tan\theta&=-\frac{15}{8}\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: If $\sin A=-\frac13$ and $\tan A<0$, find $\sec A$.

answer.worked:
$A$ is in quadrant IV, so $\sec A>0$. A reference triangle has opposite side $1$ and hypotenuse $3$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Adjacent}&=\sqrt{3^2-1^2}\\&=2\sqrt2\\\sec A&=\frac3{2\sqrt2}\\&=\frac{3\sqrt2}{4}\end{aligned}$$

$$\sin B=\frac37$$

$B$ is in quadrant II, so $\tan B<0$. A reference triangle has opposite side $3$ and hypotenuse $7$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Adjacent}&=\sqrt{7^2-3^2}\\&=2\sqrt{10}\\\tan B&=-\frac3{2\sqrt{10}}\\&=-\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{20}\end{aligned}$$

$$\cos\theta=-\frac1{\sqrt2}$$

Both cosine and sine are negative, so $\theta$ is in quadrant III and $\cot\theta>0$. A reference triangle has adjacent side $1$ and hypotenuse $\sqrt2$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Opposite}&=\sqrt{(\sqrt2)^2-1^2}\\&=1\\\cot\theta&=\frac11\\&=1\end{aligned}$$
